edit.title: ဘင်္ဂါလီတို့၏ နယ်မြေလုပွဲ
edit.mDescription:
A Burmese political book by Phyapon Nadi, first published in June 2014, whose title means 'the Bengalis' land grab'. The author calls the Rohingya 'Bengalis' and argues that they are migrants from Bangladesh trying to take over land in Rakhine State, that the Rohingya identity is a political invention, and that Rakhine risks becoming another Kashmir. It includes the author's tables of Rakhine villages in Maungdaw he says were destroyed in the 1942 violence. Later chapters on Islam, citizenship and defence are not in this file.

ဖျာပုံနဒီ ရေးသားပြီး ၂၀၁၄ ခုနှစ် ဇွန်လတွင် ပထမအကြိမ် ထုတ်ဝေသော မြန်မာဘာသာ နိုင်ငံရေးစာအုပ် ဖြစ်သည်။ စာရေးသူက ရိုဟင်ဂျာများကို “ဘင်္ဂါလီ” ဟုခေါ်ပြီး ၎င်းတို့သည် ဘင်္ဂလားဒေ့ရှ်မှ ဝင်ရောက်လာကာ ရခိုင်ပြည်နယ်ရှိ နယ်မြေကို သိမ်းယူရန် ကြိုးပမ်းနေကြောင်း၊ ရိုဟင်ဂျာ ဟူသော အမည်မှာ နိုင်ငံရေးအရ ဖန်တီးထားခြင်း ဖြစ်ကြောင်းနှင့် ရခိုင်သည် ဒုတိယ ကက်ရှ်မီးယား ဖြစ်လာနိုင်ကြောင်း စောဒကတက်သည်။ ၁၉၄၂ အရေးအခင်းတွင် ဖျက်ဆီးခံရသည်ဟု စာရေးသူ ဆိုသော မောင်တောမြို့နယ်ရှိ ရခိုင်ရွာများ၏ ဇယားများလည်း ပါဝင်သည်။ အစ္စလာမ်၊ နိုင်ငံသားဖြစ်မှုနှင့် ကာကွယ်ရေးဆိုင်ရာ နောက်ပိုင်းအခန်းများ ဤဖိုင်တွင် မပါဝင်ပါ။
Author        : Phyapon Nadi
Year          : 2014
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 36

edit.title: Rohingya Hoax
edit.mDescription:
Maung Tha Hla argues that the Rohingya are not an indigenous people of Arakan but descendants of migrants from Chittagong, presents Rohingya movements as linked to Islamist militancy and a threat to Burma's national security, and disputes Rohingya accounts of their origins.
Author        : Maung Tha Hla
Year          : 2009
Language      : English
ISBN          : 0-9726465-1-5
Pages         : 108
File Size     : 17.9 MB

edit.title: Exposing the False Incrimination of Genocide
edit.mDescription:
A book in English by the American writer Rick Heizman, first published in Yangon in May 2021. The author argues that the charge of genocide against Myanmar is false, that Rohingya militants (whom he calls Bengali Muslims) were the ones with genocidal intent, and that the media, the UN, the ICC and human rights groups such as Fortify Rights were manipulated. In 40 short articles over five chapters he draws on Myanmar's Independent Commission of Enquiry reports, newspaper clippings from 1946 to 1991 and statements he presents as from captured ARSA members.
Author        : Rick Heizman
Year          : 2021
Language      : English
Pages         : 225
File Size     : 25.8 MB

edit.title: ပါလီမန်ဒီမိုကရေစီခေတ်ရခိုင်နိုင်ငံရေးနှင့်မျက်မှောက်ခေတ်ဘူးသီးတောင်မောင်တောအခြေအနေ
edit.mDescription:
A Burmese book by Saya Khaing Myo Saung, published in Tokyo in 2010 by the Rakhine exile group Arakan Rakhitta Group, with a foreword by Dr Aye Chan. Its two parts cover Rakhine politics in the parliamentary democracy era after 1948 and the situation in Buthidaung and Maungdaw. The author argues that the British brought Chittagonian Bengali Muslims into Arakan as labourers, that they pushed out the Rakhine of Maungdaw and Buthidaung, and that the Mujahid rebellion was a separatist threat. It ends with a sketch map of Maungdaw town.

ဆရာခိုင်မျိုးစောင့် ရေးသားပြီး ဂျပန်နိုင်ငံရှိ ရခိုင်မျိုးစောင့်အုပ်စု (Arakan Rakhitta Group) က ၂၀၁၀ ခုနှစ်တွင် ထုတ်ဝေသော မြန်မာဘာသာ စာအုပ်ဖြစ်ပြီး ဒေါက်တာအေးချမ်း၏ အမှာစာ ပါဝင်သည်။ အပိုင်းနှစ်ပိုင်းတွင် ၁၉၄၈ နောက်ပိုင်း ပါလီမန်ဒီမိုကရေစီခေတ် ရခိုင်နိုင်ငံရေးနှင့် ဘူးသီးတောင်၊ မောင်တော အခြေအနေကို ဖော်ပြထားသည်။ စာရေးသူက ဗြိတိသျှတို့သည် စစ်တကောင်း ဘင်္ဂါလီမွတ်စလင်များကို လယ်ယာလုပ်သားများအဖြစ် ရခိုင်ပြည်သို့ ခေါ်ဆောင်လာခဲ့ကြောင်း၊ ၎င်းတို့က မောင်တောနှင့် ဘူးသီးတောင်ရှိ ရခိုင်များကို ဖယ်ရှားခဲ့ကြောင်းနှင့် မူဂျာဟစ်သူပုန်မှာ ခွဲထွက်ရေး ခြိမ်းခြောက်မှု ဖြစ်ကြောင်း စောဒကတက်သည်။ နောက်ဆုံးတွင် မောင်တောမြို့ မြေပုံကြမ်း ပါဝင်သည်။
Author        : ဆရာခိုင်မျိုးစောင့် (Saya Khaing Myo Saung)
Year          : 2010
Language      : Burmese
Pages         : 67
File Size     : 48.0 MB

edit.title: Influx Virus Rohingya
edit.mDescription:
Influx Viruses - The Illegal Muslims in Arakan, a 2005 book by U Shwe Zan, a former immigration officer in Arakan, and the historian Dr Aye Chan, published by Arakanese in United States. The authors argue that the Rohingya are illegal Bengali Muslim immigrants rather than an ethnic group of Burma. U Shwe Zan's essay traces Muslim migration from the Mrauk-U period to the 1980s, and Aye Chan's essay, The Development of a Muslim Enclave in Arakan, covers colonial-era migration and communal violence with British census tables. A longer Burmese section follows.
Authors       : U Shwe Zan and Dr. Aye Chan
Year          : 2005
Language      : English and Burmese
ISBN          : 0-9728698-4-0
Pages         : 77
File Size     : 0.5 MB

edit.title: မြန်မာ့စွယ်စုံကျမ်း အတွဲ (၉) အပိုင်း (က)
edit.mDescription:
Volume 9, Part A of the Myanmar Encyclopedia (Myanma Swezon Kyan), the Burmese-language general encyclopedia compiled by the Burma Translation Society (Sarpay Beikman) in Rangoon and first printed in 1964. It has alphabetical entries from Mahaw to U Maung Gyi on Burmese and world subjects, such as the Mahosadha Jataka, Mussolini and Mexico, with photographs and maps. It opens with a guide to using the encyclopedia and its alphabetical order.

မြန်မာနိုင်ငံ ဘာသာပြန်စာပေအသင်း (စာပေဗိမာန်) က ပြုစုထုတ်ဝေသော မြန်မာ့စွယ်စုံကျမ်း အတွဲ ၉၊ အပိုင်း (က) ဖြစ်ပြီး ၁၉၆၄ ခုနှစ်တွင် ပထမအကြိမ် ပုံနှိပ်ခဲ့သည်။ "မဟော" မှ "ဦးမောင်ကြီး" အထိ အက္ခရာစဉ်အလိုက် ခေါင်းစဉ်များ ပါဝင်ပြီး မဟောသဓဇာတ်တော်၊ မူဆိုလီနီ၊ မက္ကဆီကိုနိုင်ငံ စသည့် မြန်မာနှင့် ကမ္ဘာ့အကြောင်းအရာများကို ဓာတ်ပုံများ၊ မြေပုံများဖြင့် ရှင်းပြထားသည်။ စာအုပ်အစတွင် စွယ်စုံကျမ်းကို အသုံးပြုပုံနှင့် အက္ခရာစဉ်ဇယား ပါဝင်သည်။
Author        : Burma Translation Society
Editor        : U Myat Soe
Year          : 1964

Pages         : 261

edit.title: A Bachelor Girl in Burma
edit.mDescription:
A light, personal travel account by G. E. Mitton, a young unmarried Englishwoman who visited Burma, published in London in 1907. She describes Rangoon and the Shwe Dagon Pagoda, the home life of Burmese women, Moulmein, Mandalay, and journeys north towards Bhamo and the China road through the Irrawaddy defiles, as well as pwe performances and a trip on a cargo boat. It has 95 illustrations from photographs, mostly taken by the author.
Author        : G. E. Mitton
Year          : 1907
Language      : English
Pages         : 403
File Size     : 10.0 MB

edit.title: A Burmese Loneliness: A Tale of Travel in Burma, the Southern Shan States and Keng Tung
edit.mDescription:
A travel book by Captain C. M. Enriquez, an Indian Army officer serving with the Burma Military Police, published in Calcutta in 1918. Written during a lonely posting at Keng Tung in the Southern Shan States, it describes the town's festivals, market and shrines, the Shan people, Loimwe, and the frontiers with French Indo-China along the Mekong, Siam and China. Later chapters cover local arts and industries and the author's thoughts on Burma. It has a map and illustrations.
Author        : C. M. Enriquez
Year          : 1918
Language      : English
Pages         : 384
File Size     : 13.6 MB

edit.title: A Burmese Wonderland: A Tale of Travel in Lower and Upper Burma
edit.mDescription:
A travel book by Major C. M. Enriquez of the Kachin Rifles, published in Calcutta in 1922, mixing travel with history and folklore. Book One covers Lower Burma — the Kyaik-hti-yo pagoda, Thaton, the Talaings (Mon) and Karens, the Salween River, Tenasserim and Arakan. Book Two covers Upper Burma — the Pyu, Pagan and King Kyanzittha, Mount Popa and the Lower Chindwin, with chapters on General Bandula, Burmese military history, Buddhism, the old monarchy and the country beyond Mandalay.
Author        : C. M. Enriquez
Year          : 1922
Language      : English
Pages         : 324
File Size     : 13.8 MB

edit.title: A Civil Servant in Burma
edit.mDescription:
The memoir of Sir Herbert Thirkell White, who spent more than thirty years in the Burma civil service and became its Lieutenant-Governor, published in London in 1913. He tells of official life from the late 1870s, service on the frontier, the British capture of Mandalay in 1885 and the first years after the annexation of Upper Burma, a visit to the Shan States, a boundary commission and his last years on the Chief Court. There are also chapters on Burmese life and character and on Buddhism, with photographs, a glossary and an index.
Author        : Sir Herbert Thirkell White
Year          : 1913
Language      : English
Pages         : 368
File Size     : 15.3 MB

edit.title: A Concise Account of the Kingdom of Pegu
edit.mDescription:
A short account of the kingdom of Pegu in Lower Burma by William Hunter, a surgeon with the East India Company, printed in Calcutta in 1785 and based on a voyage made there around 1782. Its seven chapters describe the climate, the Peguers (Mon) and Burmans, their religion, government, manners and customs, and the trade in teak, tin, beeswax, petroleum and other goods. An appendix asks why sheep grow different fleeces in different climates, and the book ends with a description of the cave temples at Elephanta, Ambola and Canara in western India.
Author        : William Hunter
Year          : 1785
Language      : English
Pages         : 153
File Size     : 133.3 MB

edit.title: A Description of the Burmese Empire
edit.mDescription:
An account of the Burmese kingdom by Father Sangermano, an Italian Catholic missionary who lived in Rangoon and Ava from 1783 to 1808, compiled mainly from Burmese writings and translated from his manuscript by William Tandy. Published in 1833, it covers Burmese cosmology, the royal chronicle and history of the kings, the king and his court, officials, taxes and army, Buddhism and its monks, the character, customs, literature and calendar of the people, trade and money, and ends with a summary of the Burmese law code (Dhammathat).
Author        : Vincenzo Sangermano
Translator    : William Tandy
Year          : 1833
Language      : English
Pages         : 242
File Size     : 7.8 MB

edit.title: A Narrative of the First Burmese War, 1824–26
edit.mDescription:
An official history of the First Anglo-Burmese War of 1824–26 by G. W. De Rhé-Philipe of the Government of India's Military Department, printed in Calcutta in 1905 and built around the official reports and despatches. It traces the war's origins on the Chittagong–Arakan frontier after the Burmese conquest of Arakan, the fighting in Assam, Kachar and Chittagong, the expedition to Rangoon, the conquest of Tenasserim, Arakan and Assam, the advance into Ava and Pegu, and the peace of Yandabo. Appendices give short biographies of officers and a roll of British officers killed, wounded or captured.
Author        : G. W. De Rhé-Philipe
Year          : 1905
Language      : English
Pages         : 462
File Size     : 205.6 MB

edit.title: A Narrative of the Mission to the Court of Ava in 1855
edit.mDescription:
Captain Henry Yule's account of the 1855 British mission, led by Major Arthur Phayre, from Lord Dalhousie to King Mindon at Amarapura, published in London in 1858 with many illustrations. It follows the journey up the Irrawaddy, the ruins of Pagan, life at the royal capital and excursions around it. Later chapters cover Burma's dealings with Western nations, its history from 1826 to 1853, religion, government, army and revenue, geography and population, and the Shan states, with appendices on geology, trade, royal edicts, architecture and languages.
Author        : Henry Yule
Year          : 1858
Language      : English
Pages         : 474
File Size     : 28.3 MB

edit.title: A Parson's Holiday: A Tour in India, Burma and Ceylon
edit.mDescription:
A travel account by W. Osborn B. Allen, vicar of Shirburn in Oxfordshire, of his tour of India, Burma and Ceylon in the winter of 1882–83, printed at Tenby in 1885. Most chapters describe India, from Bombay and Poona to Delhi, Agra, Lucknow, Benares, Calcutta, Madras and Tinnevelly, with close attention to Christian missions and schools. Two chapters cover Burma — its history, Rangoon, Buddhism, pagodas and monks, missionaries, Prome, Moulmein and Pegu — and the last covers Ceylon and the voyage home.
Author        : William Osborne Bird Allen
Year          : 1885
Language      : English
Pages         : 246
File Size     : 12.3 MB

edit.title: A Personal Narrative of Two Years' Imprisonment in Burmah, 1824–26
edit.mDescription:
The memoir of Henry Gouger, a British merchant who went to trade at the Burmese court and was imprisoned at Ava for two years when the First Anglo-Burmese War began, published in London in 1860. He describes the voyage up the Irrawaddy, life at Amarapura and Ava and the royal family, then his arrest and the death prison, where he was held in fetters with the American missionary Dr. Judson and others. It ends with his release, Rangoon after the peace treaty, and a visit to Amherst.
Author        : Henry Gouger
Year          : 1860
Language      : English
Pages         : 366
File Size     : 14.3 MB

edit.title: A Political History of the Extraordinary Events Which Led to the Burmese War
edit.mDescription:
A contemporary critique of the causes of the First Anglo-Burmese War by Captain W. White, published in London in 1827 and based mainly on Indian government records laid before Parliament. The author questions the official view that the Burmese were the only aggressors. He traces early British contact with Burma, the Burmese conquest of Arakan and the flight of tens of thousands of Arakanese refugees into British Chittagong, their raids back into Arakan, disputes over Assam and Shahpuri Island, and the outbreak of war in 1824.
Author        : William White
Year          : 1827
Language      : English
Pages         : 201
File Size     : 10.8 MB

edit.title: A Short History of Burma
edit.mDescription:
A concise history of Burma written for students by S. W. Cocks of the Indian Educational Service, in the revised second edition published in London in 1919. It runs from the early Prome kingdom, Thaton and Pagan through the Shan, Ava, Pegu and Toungoo periods and King Bayinnaung, to the Alaungpaya dynasty, the wars with Britain and the annexation under King Thibaw. Separate chapters cover Arakan and society and government under the last dynasty, with a chronology, a family tree of the kings and a map.
Author        : S. W. Cocks
Year          : 1919
Language      : English
Pages         : 199
File Size     : 5.5 MB

edit.title: A Year on the Irrawaddy
edit.mDescription:
Light personal sketches by a captain's wife, signed E. M. P-B., who spent about eighteen months aboard an oil steamer on the Irrawaddy commanded by her husband, published in Rangoon in 1911. Part One follows a typical trip from Rangoon through the Bassein creek and past Myanaung, Prome and Thayetmyo up to Nyaunghla, with chapters on accidents, the crew and a day ashore. Part Two describes the river month by month, with fogs, heat and the rains, a trip to Mandalay, a morning at Mingun and a journey on a mail boat. It has eight illustrations.
Author        : E. M. Powell-Brown
Year          : 1911
Language      : English
Pages         : 274
File Size     : 44.4 MB

edit.title: Across Chrysê, Vol. I
edit.mDescription:
The first of two volumes in which Archibald R. Colquhoun, an engineer in the Indian Public Works, tells of his 1881–82 journey of exploration through the southern Chinese border lands, looking for a trade route between China and British Burma. Published in London in 1883, this volume follows the boat journey from Canton up the West River through Kwangsi province towards Yunnan, describing towns, trade, mines, opium, boatmen, officials, temples and the damage left by the Taiping rebellion. It has maps and many illustrations.
Author        : Archibald R. Colquhoun
Year          : 1883
Language      : English
Pages         : 483
File Size     : 21.6 MB

edit.title: Across Chrysê, Vol. II
edit.mDescription:
The second volume of Archibald R. Colquhoun's account of his 1881–82 journey from Canton to Mandalay, published in London in 1883. It crosses Yunnan from Lin-an and the Red River to Ssu-mao on the edge of the Shan country, then north to Tali, over the Mekong and Salween to Teng-yueh, and through the Kachin hills to Bhamo, ending with the steamer trip to Mandalay and Rangoon. Along the way it discusses trade routes between Burma and China, the Muslim rebellion in Yunnan, Margary's murder, and the Lolo, Shan and Kachin peoples.
Author        : Archibald R. Colquhoun
Year          : 1883
Language      : English
Pages         : 494
File Size     : 27.6 MB

edit.title: Amongst the Shans
edit.mDescription:
Archibald Ross Colquhoun's account of his journey in 1879 with the British mission to Siam, from Moulmein in British Burma across the Salween and the Karen hills to Zimmé (Chiang Mai) in the Shan country, and down the Menam to Bangkok, published in 1885. Chapters describe the Karens, Lawas, Kachins and other hill peoples, Shan towns and customs, trade, slavery and government in Burma and Siam, and plans for railways. It opens with Terrien de Lacouperie's essay on the origins of the Shan race and ends with Holt S. Hallett's history of the Shans.
Author        : Archibald R. Colquhoun
Year          : 1885
Language      : English
Pages         : 462
File Size     : 29.7 MB

edit.title: An Account of an Embassy to the Kingdom of Ava in 1795
edit.mDescription:
Major Michael Symes's account of the British embassy sent by the Governor-General of India to the Burmese king in 1795, published in London in 1800. It opens with a historical memoir of the Burmese kingdom, including the Burmese conquest of Arakan in 1784 and a description of Arakan and its peoples. The narrative then follows the mission from the Andaman Islands to Rangoon and Pegu and up the Irrawaddy past Prome and Pagan to the capital, describing the court, religion, laws, army, trade and customs, with plates and appendices.
Author        : Michael Symes
Year          : 1800
Language      : English
Pages         : 536
File Size     : 20.0 MB

edit.title: An Account of the Burman Empire
edit.mDescription:
A compilation printed in Calcutta in 1852 that gathers the main passages on Burma from earlier writers such as Symes, Cox, Canning, Leyden and Buchanan. It covers the country's geography, climate, products, government, army, laws, religion, languages and history, then describes its cities and towns, among them Amarapura, Ava, Pagan, Rangoon, Pegu and Arakan, and the tribes in and around the kingdom, taken from the missionary Howard Malcom. It ends with Henry G. Bell's narrative of the First Anglo-Burmese War of 1824–26.
Author        : Compiled from Symes, Canning, Cox, Leyden and Buchanan; narrative by Henry G. Bell
Year          : 1852
Language      : English

edit.title: An English Girl's First Impressions of Burmah
edit.mDescription:
A humorous account by Beth Ellis of her visit to Burma as a young Englishwoman, first published in 1899. She describes the voyage out through the Suez Canal, Rangoon, the road to Mandalay and the journey into the hills to an up-country station she calls Remyo. Later chapters sketch the European residents, the Burmese, social life, adventures, wild animals and sport, and the voyage home. This copy is the Project Gutenberg e-book edition.
Author        : Beth Ellis
Year          : 1899
Language      : English
Pages         : 92
File Size     : 1.0 MB

edit.title: An Old Soldier's Memories
edit.mDescription:
The memoirs of S. H. Jones-Parry, an officer of the 1st Madras Fusiliers, published in London in 1897. Five chapters cover his service in the Second Anglo-Burmese War of 1852–53 — Rangoon and the great pagoda, the capture and two defences of Pegu, a jungle march to Shwegyin and garrison life at Toungoo — with remarks on the Burmese people and religion. The rest of the book covers his youth, the Crimean War with the Turkish Contingent, the relief of Lucknow during the Indian Mutiny, and later life in Wales.
Author        : S. H. Jones-Parry
Year          : 1897
Language      : English
Pages         : 314
File Size     : 16.3 MB

edit.title: Big Game Shooting in Upper Burma
edit.mDescription:
A hunting guide by Major G. P. Evans of the Indian Army, based on his own years of hunting on foot in the Upper and Lower Chindwin, Shwebo, Sagaing, Meiktila, Magwe and Yamethin districts. Chapters cover the elephant, gaur, banteng, rhinoceros, tiger, leopard, Malay bear, serow and several kinds of deer, followed by advice on trackers, rifles, kit, camp and servants, a list of hunting places and a glossary of Burmese jungle words. This copy is the 1912 reprint of the 1911 London edition.
Author        : G. P. Evans
Year          : 1912
Language      : English
Pages         : 264

It covers their origins and migrations, dialects, villages and houses, dress, character, chiefs and customary law, farming, crafts and slavery, weapons and warfare, music and dances, myths and traditions, divination and spirit (nat) worship, and birth, marriage and funeral ceremonies. It ends with their future and appendices on kinship terms and family names.
Author        : Ola Hanson
Year          : 1913
Language      : English
Pages         : 284
File Size     : 16.1 MB

edit.title: The Karen Apostle: Memoir of Ko Thah-byu, the First Karen Convert
edit.mDescription:
A missionary biography of Ko Tha Byu, the first Karen convert to Christianity, by Francis Mason of the American Baptist mission to the Karens. It tells of his early life, baptism and preaching journeys around Tavoy, Moulmein, Rangoon and Pegu, Burmese persecution of the Karens, and his last journey to Arakan, where he died. A final chapter argues for the Karen mission, and an appendix describes Karen history, geography, traditions, precepts, funeral rites and prophets. It is written from a missionary viewpoint.
Author        : Francis Mason
Editor        : H. J. Ripley
Year          : 1847
Language      : English
Pages         : 144
File Size     : 6.1 MB

edit.title: The Karen People of Burma
edit.mDescription:
A study of the Karen people in anthropology and ethnology by H. I. Marshall, an American Baptist missionary in Burma, published by Ohio State University in 1922. Its five parts cover general topics (where the Karens live, their origins, physical and moral traits, language, dress and calendar), domestic life (houses, food, farming, hunting, weaving and bronze drums), social life (laws, warfare, music, birth, marriage and funerals), religious life (beliefs, spirits, offerings, magic and taboos), and the growth of Christianity among them. It has a glossary, bibliography and index.
Author        : Harry Ignatius Marshall
Year          : 1922
Language      : English
Pages         : 357
File Size     : 5.1 MB

edit.title: The Land of the White Elephant
edit.mDescription:
A travel narrative by the American writer Frank Vincent of his journey through Burma, Siam, Cambodia and Cochin-China in 1871–72. The Burma chapters cover Rangoon, the voyage up the Irrawaddy past the oil wells and Pagan, Mandalay and an audience with King Mindon, the royal white elephant, Bhamo and the old trade route to China, and Moulmein. Later chapters describe Penang, Malacca, Singapore, Bangkok and the Siamese court, the ruins of Angkor in Cambodia, and Saigon. It has a map, plans and illustrations.
Author        : Frank Vincent
Year          : 1873
Language      : English
Pages         : 387
File Size     : 12.3 MB

edit.title: The Loyal Karens of Burma
edit.mDescription:
An account of the Karen people by Donald Mackenzie Smeaton of the Bengal Civil Service, written soon after the Third Anglo-Burmese War. A long introduction praises the Karens for helping the British against the Burmese resistance of 1885–87. Chapters then describe Karen origins, language and appearance, customs, farming and the harvest goddess, folklore and fireside stories, national character, their legendary ancestor, traditional religion, the American Baptist mission among them, and British policy toward the Karens, with an appendix.
Author        : Donald Mackenzie Smeaton
Year          : 1887
Language      : English
Pages         : 312
File Size     : 13.9 MB

edit.title: The Pacification of Burma
edit.mDescription:
A first-hand account by Sir Charles Crosthwaite, Chief Commissioner of Burma from 1887 to 1890, of how the British imposed their rule on Upper Burma after the annexation of 1885. He describes the administration and Mandalay, campaigns against armed resistance (called dacoits), disarmament, the replacement of soldiers by police, and operations in Minbu, Myingyan and Magwe. Later chapters cover the Shan States, the Karenni and Trans-Salween states, Bhamo and Mogaung, the Chins and the Chin-Lushai campaign. It has photographs, maps and an index.
Author        : Sir Charles Crosthwaite
Year          : 1912
Language      : English
Pages         : 440
File Size     : 28.0 MB

edit.title: The Province of Burma, Vol. I
edit.mDescription:
The first volume of a detailed report on British colonial rule in Burma, prepared by Alleyne Ireland for the University of Chicago as part of a series on colonial administration in the Far East. Its ten chapters describe the country, the British acquisition of Burma, the people, the system of government, general administration, the civil service, the courts, the police, prisons and education. Appendices reprint treaties with Burma and give 1901 census tables, civil service rules, climate data and statistics on justice, crime, jails and schools.
Author        : Alleyne Ireland
Year          : 1907
Language      : English
Pages         : 558
File Size     : 38.6 MB

edit.title: The Province of Burma, Vol. II
edit.mDescription:
The second volume of Alleyne Ireland's report on British colonial administration in Burma, prepared for the University of Chicago. It covers the financial system and currency, land revenue and land tenure, forests, public works, municipal and village administration, health and hospitals, harbours, the administration of the Shan States and the Chin Hills, and trade and shipping. Long appendices give statistics on finance, revenue, opium, forests, health and trade, a bibliography of Burma (with a section on Arakan and the Arakanese), a glossary and an index to both volumes.
Author        : Alleyne Ireland
Year          : 1907
Language      : English
Pages         : 530
File Size     : 52.4 MB

edit.title: The Recent Operations of the British Forces at Rangoon and Martaban
edit.mDescription:
An eyewitness account of the opening of the Second Anglo-Burmese War in 1852 by the Rev. Thomas Turner Baker, chaplain of the British warship Fox, published after he died of cholera at Rangoon in April 1852. It reviews British relations with the Burmese court since the 1826 Treaty of Yandabo and the dispute that led to war, then describes the capture of Martaban and the attack on Rangoon and the Shwedagon Pagoda, with official despatches, casualty lists and illustrations.
Author        : Thomas Turner Baker
Year          : 1852
Language      : English
Pages         : 103
File Size     : 1.8 MB

edit.title: The Romantic East: Burma, Assam, & Kashmir
edit.mDescription:
A travel book by Walter Del Mar describing a tour of Burma, Assam and Kashmir, with 64 photographs. About half the book is on Burma, covering Burmese customs, religion and women, Rangoon and the Shwedagon, the journey up the Irrawaddy to Bhamo, the peoples of Upper Burma, Mandalay and its palace, the Gokteik viaduct, Moulmein, and a coastal voyage from Rangoon to Chittagong with New Year's Day at Akyab. The rest covers Assam's tea industry and a long journey to Srinagar and the Kashmir valley.
Author        : Walter Del Mar
Year          : 1906
Language      : English
Pages         : 368
File Size     : 15.9 MB

edit.title: The Second Burmese War: A Narrative of the Operations at Rangoon in 1852
edit.mDescription:
The first of W. F. B. Laurie's eyewitness narratives of the Second Anglo-Burmese War, written in Rangoon in 1852 by a lieutenant of the Madras Artillery. After a sketch of earlier relations and how the Burmese 'provoked' a second war (in the author's words), it follows the force from Madras to Rangoon, the naval operations at Rangoon and Dalla, the landing, the assault on the Shwedagon Pagoda, life among the temples, Buddhism, the capture of Bassein, the attack on Martaban, and the questions of Pegu and Prome. Supplementary notes and an appendix follow.
Author        : W. F. B. Laurie
Year          : 1853
Language      : English
Pages         : 317
File Size     : 5.3 MB

edit.title: The Shans, Vol. I
edit.mDescription:
A history and description of the Shan (Tai) peoples by W. W. Cochrane, an American Baptist missionary, first published by the Government of Burma in Rangoon in 1915. It discusses the origin of the Shans, their history in Yunnan up to the 13th century, the Shans on the Mekong, and the Shans of Burma (the Mao kingdom) from legendary times to the present. Later chapters cover the Shan language and script, traditional beliefs, Shan Buddhism, and Christianity. It has photographs and an index. Only this first volume was published.
Author        : W. W. Cochrane
Year          : 1981
Language      : English
ISBN          : 0-404-16805-1
Pages         : 278
File Size     : 11.6 MB

edit.title: The Silken East, Vol. I
edit.mDescription:
A richly illustrated record of life and travel in Burma by V. C. Scott O'Connor, a former official there, in the one-volume new edition introduced by Sir Harcourt Butler. After chapters on the country and its peoples, it describes Rangoon and the Shwedagon, journeys on the Irrawaddy to Bhamo, Prome, Pagan and Mandalay, the Chindwin, the delta, Mergui and the southern coast, the Salween and Sittang rivers, and the ruby mines at Mogok. It has about 200 illustrations, including coloured plates.
Author        : V. C. Scott O'Connor
Year          : 1928
Language      : English
Pages         : 410
File Size     : 28.2 MB

edit.title: The Silken East, Vol. II
edit.mDescription:
The second volume of the first edition of The Silken East, a richly illustrated record of life and travel in Burma by V. C. Scott O'Connor, then Comptroller of Assam. It continues the journey on the Chindwin river, then covers the Irrawaddy delta, the southern coast with Mergui, its pearling town and archipelago, and Moulmein, voyages on the Salween and Yunzalin rivers, the Paung-laung hills, the Sittang river and the canal to Pegu, and the ruby mines of Mogok, ending with an index.
Author        : V. C. Scott O'Connor
Year          : 1904
Language      : English
Pages         : 457
File Size     : 7.6 MB

edit.title: The Soul of a People
edit.mDescription:
A sympathetic portrait of Burmese Buddhist life by H. Fielding Hall, a British official who lived in Burma around the time of the 1885 annexation. In 23 short chapters he describes everyday beliefs, the life of the Buddha and the path to peace, the Burmese at war, government, crime and punishment, monks and monasteries, prayer, festivals, the position of women, marriage and divorce, manners, the idea that all life is one, death and rebirth. This copy is a 1909 reprint of the 1898 book.
Author        : H. Fielding Hall
Year          : 1909
Language      : English
Pages         : 314
File Size     : 18.2 MB

edit.title: Travels in South-Eastern Asia
edit.mDescription:
An account of the travels of Howard Malcom, sent by the American Baptist mission board in the 1830s to visit its missions in Asia (second edition, two volumes in one). Part I covers Moulmein, Tavoy, Mergui, Rangoon, the Irrawaddy and Ava, then Chittagong, Cox's Bazar, Akyab, Kyaukpyu and Ramree in Arakan. Part II is a detailed account of the Burman empire, including history, land, people, customs, government, trade and Buddhism. Parts III and IV cover India, Malaya, Siam and China, with essays and tables on missions.
Author        : Howard Malcom
Year          : 1839
Language      : English
Pages         : 616
File Size     : 36.9 MB

edit.title: Travels of Doctor and Madame Helfer, Vol. 2
edit.mDescription:
The second volume of the memoir of Pauline, Countess Nostitz (formerly Madame Helfer), translated from German by Mrs. George Sturge. It follows her and her husband, the naturalist Dr. J. W. Helfer, from Persia to Calcutta and then to British Tenasserim in 1837–40, with expeditions up the Salween river and to the Three Pagodas Pass, life on their plantation at Mergui, and his explorations in the Mergui Archipelago, where he was killed. The rest of the book tells of her later life in India, Egypt, London, Prussia and Bohemia.
Author        : Pauline Nostitz
Translator    : Mrs. George Sturge
Year          : 1878
Language      : English
Pages         : 368
File Size     : 21.4 MB

edit.title: Twenty-six Years in Burmah
edit.mDescription:
A biography of the American Baptist missionary Joseph G. Binney, written by his widow from his letters and journals. It covers his childhood, conversion and pastorates in New England and Savannah, his call to Burma in 1843 and arrival at Moulmein in 1844, and his long work training Karen preachers and teachers, above all at the Karen Theological Seminary in Rangoon. Later chapters describe his visits home, his final journey back to Burma, his death on that voyage, memorial services in Rangoon and tributes from colleagues.
Author        : Mrs. Joseph G. Binney
Year          : 1880
Language      : English
Pages         : 404
File Size     : 19.4 MB

edit.title: Wanderings in Burma
edit.mDescription:
A traveller's guide to Burma by George W. Bird of the Burma Educational Department, with illustrations and maps. The introduction gives a geographical summary, the Shan States, languages, the Burmese language, religion, chief towns, a historical summary, administration, a glossary and statistics. The rest describes 24 routes, such as Rangoon and its surroundings, Pegu, Prome, Bassein, Moulmein, Tavoy and Mergui, the coastal steamer to Akyab, Mandalay and the old capitals, Pagan, Bhamo, Myitkyina and Maymyo.
Author        : George W. Bird
Year          : 1897
Language      : English
Pages         : 611
File Size     : 7.8 MB

edit.title: Wild Sports of Burma and Assam
edit.mDescription:
A hunting and natural history book by Colonel F. T. Pollok and W. S. Thom, a police officer in Burma, with illustrations and maps. Pollok's part on Lower Burma describes Burmese habits and customs and then the game animals, including tigers, leopards, buffaloes, rhinoceros, gaur, deer and elephants, with jungle trips. Thom's part on Upper Burma covers the journey from Rangoon to Mandalay, the Ruby Mines, elephants, gaur and wild cattle. Short closing parts deal with Assam and the Khasi and Jaintia hills.
Author        : F. T. Pollok and W. S. Thom
Year          : 1900
Language      : English
Pages         : 537
File Size     : 95.3 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Class One
edit.mDescription:
A Rohingya reading textbook for school pupils, written in the Hanifi script and produced by the Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee. After a foreword and a contents page listing 21 lessons, each lesson has an illustrated reading passage, including animal fables such as the fox and the stork, family, food, school and daily life. Every lesson is followed by exercises with questions, fill-in-the-blanks and word matching, and the book ends with a poem.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 57
File Size     : 15.4 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Science
edit.mDescription:
A picture-based science textbook for young pupils, written in Rohingya in the Hanifi script and produced by the Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee. It covers living and non-living things, the parts of a tree from roots to fruit, seeds and food plants, plants in different places such as deserts, mountains and water, and groups of animals including mammals, birds, reptiles, frogs, fish and insects. Later lessons show farm animals and sources of fuel, and each lesson has picture exercises and short questions.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 26

edit.title: Rohingya Quaida
edit.mDescription:
An illustrated Rohingya alphabet primer (qaida) in the Hanifi script, part of the Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee school series. It opens with charts of the letters, vowel signs and numerals, then teaches each vowel sign with syllable tables and picture words such as animals, fruit and household objects. Later lessons are short illustrated reading passages, for example about school, the mosque and prayer, greetings and birds, and a poem.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 22
File Size     : 4.3 MB

edit.title: Aasan Kaida
edit.mDescription:
An easy alphabet primer (aasan kaida) for learning to read Rohingya in the Hanifi script, printed in full colour. After a contents page and charts of the letters and numerals, each page teaches a few letters with photographs, example words and writing practice. The later lessons are short reading passages on Islam, greetings, home, animals and farming, and on Rohingya history, including Jafar Hussain Kawwal, founder of the Mujahid movement in Arakan. It ends with question pages and a letter exercise.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 36
File Size     : 12.4 MB

edit.title: English to Rohingya Dictionary
edit.mDescription:
An English to Rohingya dictionary from the Rohingya Language Committee. English headwords from A to Z, each marked as noun, verb, adjective or adverb, are listed in two columns with their Rohingya meanings in the Hanifi script, about 5,500 entries in all. Many entries are everyday and official words, and some are religious terms such as ablution, zakat and Zamzam. A foreword and an afterword, both in Hanifi, frame the word list.
Writer        : Zuban Committee
Language      : English and Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 60
File Size     : 5.6 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Glossary
edit.mDescription:
An illustrated phrasebook from the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Malaysia, funded by European Union Humanitarian Aid, to help aid workers talk with Rohingya refugees. Words and phrases are set out in three columns, English, Malay and Rohingya in the Roman alphabet. Its 19 sections cover greetings, interviews and travel history, protection, requests, the body, hospital visits, symptoms, treatment and COVID-19, feelings and psychology, gender-based violence, family, daily routine, religion, food, and numbers, days and months.
Author        : International Organization for Migration (IOM)
Year          : 2021
Language      : English, Malay and Rohingya (Latin script)
Pages         : 105
File Size     : 11.9 MB

edit.title: Aasan Qawaid: The Easy Grammar of Rohingya Language
edit.mDescription:
A grammar of the Rohingya language written in an Urdu-style Arabic script by Ustad Muhammad Sultan, son of Maulana Muhammad Abdullah, from Maungdaw. After a preface on language and writing, it sets out the alphabet and vowel marks and explains letter sounds such as the nasal nun and the forms of waw and ya. Most of the book is tables of verbs, pronouns and tenses (with English labels such as Past Indefinite), full conjugations, imperatives and negatives, participles, and lists of words with their meanings.
Author        : Ustad Muhammad Sultan bin Maulana Muhammad Abdullah
Language      : Rohingya (Arabic script)
Pages         : 97
File Size     : 21.4 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Language Book 3
edit.mDescription:
A Rohingya language reader for older primary pupils (book 3), written in the Hanifi script and published by the Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee. Its illustrated reading lessons include Mecca and the Kaaba, the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, the Quran, teeth and keeping them clean, animal fables such as the monkey and the crocodile, the air and its gases, nature and the seasons, and lives of historical and religious figures. After each lesson come exercises with word meanings, questions and fill-in-the-blanks.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 60
File Size     : 14.0 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Language Book 4
edit.mDescription:
A Rohingya language reader (book 4) for upper primary pupils, typed in the Hanifi script and issued by the Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee. Its illustrated reading lessons include the Prophet's Mosque, birds and forests, rice growing, animal stories, and Rohingya and Arakan history with dates such as 1784, 1824, 1948 and 1982, as well as lives of Rohingya figures and early European accounts of Arakan by writers such as Joao de Barros. Each lesson ends with word meanings, questions and fill-in-the-blank exercises.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 78
File Size     : 17.3 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Zuban to Arabic (Handwritten, 1988)
edit.mDescription:
A picture word book for learning Arabic and English through Rohingya, titled on its back cover Learn Arabic and English with the Rohangia Language. After a foreword, pictures of the Quran, the Kaaba and the Prophet's Mosque, and a chart matching the Hanifi letters to Arabic letters and Latin sounds, each page has six everyday words with a drawing, such as woman, train, school, horse, bus, cat and apple, given in Arabic, English and Rohingya in the Hanifi script. It ends with Arabic and English alphabet charts.
Year          : 1988
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script), Arabic and English
Pages         : 32
File Size     : 10.0 MB

edit.title: Shurur Kitab Foro (KG)
edit.mDescription:
A first reading book for kindergarten children learning Rohingya in the Hanifi script, from the Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee. After a foreword and charts of the letters and vowel signs, about nine lessons each teach one vowel sign with a syllable table, four picture words and a short word-reading box. The last part has short illustrated reading passages and poems, for example on school, the mosque and prayer, a bird, greetings and an old man with a child.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 2.8 MB

edit.title: The First Rohingya Reader
edit.mDescription:
A first English reader for Rohingya children, titled The First Reader Rohingya and English Teacher, written by Noor Alam Mohammad Ismail and published by the Rohingya Education Board. After a Hanifi letter chart, it teaches the English alphabet from A to Z with four picture words per letter, each with its Rohingya pronunciation and meaning in the Hanifi script. Later pages cover a and an, flowers, fruits and colours, family words, days and months, numbers to twenty, this and that sentences, the nursery rhyme Twinkle, Twinkle, and a saying about going early to bed.
Author        : Noor Alam Mohammad Ismail
Compiled by   : M. R. Mohammad Younus Abdur Rashid
Language      : English and Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 28
File Size     : 10.8 MB

edit.title: Rohingya English Burmese Vocabulary (Vegetables)
edit.mDescription:
A short illustrated word list of about 60 vegetables, fruits, herbs and spices, set out in a table with the Rohingya name in the Hanifi script, the English and Burmese names, and a colour photograph. It includes chilli, onion, pumpkin, cabbage, maize, ginger, mango, guava and many more. The last two pages, in Hanifi only, are picture pages that list the days of the week and the names of the months.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script), English and Burmese
Pages         : 10
File Size     : 1.1 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Foro
edit.mDescription:
A first Hanifi Rohingya reader for children, made by the Rohingya Language Council with Mukti Cox's Bazar and Children on the Edge. After a foreword and a chart of the letters and vowel signs, each page teaches two letters, each with a colour photograph, the word it starts, the word spelled out letter by letter and a short sentence. The last pages have word lists for reading practice and practice with vowel signs.
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 2.3 MB

edit.title: Rohingya Qaida (2023)
edit.mDescription:
A full-colour Hanifi Rohingya alphabet primer (qaida) for children and adult beginners, issued by the Burma Rohingya Zuban Committee and dated 15 October 2023 on its cover. After a foreword and charts of the letters, numerals and vowel signs, about 25 lessons each teach one vowel sign or spelling rule with syllable tables, word lists and dotted lines for writing practice. Later lessons explain doubled and nasal sounds and loanwords, give short reading passages and poems, and end with letters of approval from religious scholars.
Year          : 2023
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 58
File Size     : 8.1 MB

edit.title: Rohingyas and Kamans
edit.mDescription:
A short history of two Muslim communities of Arakan, the Rohingya and the Kaman, by the historian M. A. Tahir Ba Tha, compiled from his earlier magazine articles. It was distributed by the United Rohingya National League in Myitkyina.

edit.mDescription:
A book by Zaw Min Htut, president of the Burmese Rohingya Association in Japan, compiled largely from the records and writings of A. F. K. Jilani and first published in 2003. It describes decades of abuse against the Rohingya of Arakan, including the citizenship law, the refugee exoduses of 1978, 1991-92, 1996 and 1997, conditions in the Bangladesh camps, new settlements in Arakan, forced labour, limits on religious freedom and the 2001 violence in Akyab (Sittwe). edit.title: The union of Burma and ethnic Rohingyas
edit.mDescription:
A history of the Rohingya in Burmese by Zaw Min Htut, published in Tokyo by the Burmese Rohingya Association in Japan in 2001. edit.title: Aasan Masahla
edit.mDescription:
A book of easy Islamic rulings (masa'il) in Rohingya, written in the Hanifi script by Maulana Zunaid Roshid Ahmadi and published by the Rohingya Zuban Committee in 2020. After a preface opening with an Arabic praise of Allah, it is set out as numbered chapters of questions and answers, beginning with the testimony of faith quoted in Arabic and going on through belief, purification, prayer and other daily duties, with numbered lists of conditions and rules.
Author        : Maulana Zunaid Roshid Ahmadi
Year          : 2020
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 51
File Size     : 8.3 MB

edit.title: Hoittor Hadis – 70 Hadiths (سبعون حديث)
edit.mDescription:
A booklet of seventy short hadith with a Rohingya translation in the Hanifi script, titled Sab'un Hadith in Arabic. Set in two columns on each page, every hadith is printed in Arabic with its narrator, such as Abu Hurayrah, and its source, mostly Muslim or Bukhari, followed by its Rohingya translation. The sayings are brief, such as 'Do not get angry', which makes them easy to learn by heart. A preface opens the booklet.
Language      : Arabic and Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 20
File Size     : 3.6 MB

edit.title: 𐴀𐴞𐴀𐴁𐴠𐴑𐴝𐴉𐴡𐴌𐴢 𐴔𐴡𐴏𐴝𐴓𐴝𐴤
edit.mDescription:
A short book of Islamic rulings (masa'il) in Rohingya, written in the Hanifi script and published by the Rohingya National Education Board at the start of Ramadan 2023. The cover quotes the Quran verse on purifying the House of Allah for those who circle it and those who stay there in worship. The text is arranged under headed sections and numbered points, each ruling backed by a reference to the Quran or to hadith collections such as Bukhari and Muslim, and it ends with closing prayers in Arabic.
Author        : Maulana Muhammad Hubaib bin Abu Tahir
Year          : 2023
Language      : Rohingya (Hanifi script)
Pages         : 14
File Size     : 5.8 MB
